chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:
Beware of wrapping oneself in al-ṣammāʾ. I said: And what is wrapping oneself in al-ṣammāʾ? He said: It is that you insert the garment from beneath your side and place it over one shoulder.

key_terms.إِيَّاكَ: a warning expression meaning 'beware of' or 'avoid'
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or cloth being worn
key_terms.الصَّمَّاءِ: the specific type of wrap being warned against
key_terms.الِالْتِحَافَ: wrapping oneself in a garment in a particular manner
key_terms.جَنَاحِكَ: your side or flank, under which the garment is drawn

ai.seo_question: What does al-tiḥāf al-ṣammāʾ mean in a hadith about clothing in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith prohibits or discourages a particular manner of wrapping a garment in salat (prayer), known as al-tiḥāf al-ṣammāʾ. The Imam عليه السلام explains the form of this wrap, clarifying a practical ruling related to proper dress and decorum in worship.
